title: feat(openai): add explicit Agents API MVP harness

commit.messageHeadline: feat(openai): add explicit Agents API MVP harness
feat(agentsapi): use configured models in a standalone runtime package
chore(agentsapi): record standalone runtime dependencies
test(agentsapi): cover configured models and backend rejection messages
fix(agentsapi): retain SDK HTTP ownership through response cleanup
refactor(agentsapi): satisfy lint and preserve reader cleanup
test(agentsapi): isolate session creation at the SDK transport boundary
chore(agentsapi): label the standalone runtime package
style(agentsapi): format the standalone runtime modules
style(agentsapi): format structured submission failures safely
test(agentsapi): isolate provider route compatibility coverage
style(agentsapi): format provider route tests
test(openai): align Agents API route expectations
style(agentsapi): format route contract expectations
test(openai): align public API-key route artifact
refactor(agentsapi): compose the shared external harness runtime
test(agentsapi): cover native completion and cancellation receipts
style(agentsapi): format the shared harness adapter
test(agentsapi): retain cancellation when queued steering is rejected
style(agentsapi): bind owner callbacks for lint
fix(agentsapi): carry validated session target types
style(agentsapi): format validated session target projection
test(agentsapi): keep runtime fixtures within line caps
build(agentsapi): align schema dependency with base
build(agentsapi): refresh the schema dependency lock
fix(agentsapi): fence native effects with binding ownership
fix(agentsapi): dispatch shared completion hooks
fix(agentsapi): regenerate the Zod lock entry
docs(agentsapi): regenerate baseline above the merged base
docs(agentsapi): regenerate the bundled plugin inventory
docs(agentsapi): include generated plugin reference pages

Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. _Reviewed September 22, 2026, 8:44 PM ET / September 23, 2026, 00:44 UTC (Revision 19)._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes Adds an explicitly selected OpenAI Agents API plugin for persistent hosted Linux sessions, streamed replies, steering, interruption, and OpenClaw transcript integration. ## Merge readiness ✅ **Ready for maintainer review** Keep open as a useful, distinct implementation. The prior code blockers are resolved, and the new production-path evidence satisfies the outstanding authority-proof requirement. No actionable correctness or security finding remains. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `b549ee1963ac659cf8226bd96fb958cf24baa06e` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A coherent plugin implementation with strong production-path evidence and no remaining actionable findings. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): Authority-chain proof required: satisfied by real Docker Gateway execution and cancellation, plus production-client stale-owner rejection before HTTP and strict-writer rejection without transcript changes. The proven runtime matches this head; additive namespaced storage preserves existing formats. Token accounting remains explicitly best effort. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (live_output): Authority-chain proof required: satisfied by real Docker Gateway execution and cancellation, plus production-client stale-owner rejection before HTTP and strict-writer rejection without transcript changes. The proven runtime matches this head; additive namespaced storage preserves existing formats. Token accounting remains explicitly best effort. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 10 items | Reviewed introduction boundary: Reviewed the complete introduced patch from the verified merge base to the original PR head. Base-only test changes were excluded from PR ownership; the stale test merge was not used to infer removals.
Current-main necessity: The fetched main tree has no extensions/agentsapi plugin, and its OpenAI runtime documentation describes the existing OpenClaw and Codex routes. The merged prerequisite supplies shared coordination rather than this hosted backend.
Release boundary: The supplied latest-release revision also contains no extensions/agentsapi plugin; no shipped replacement was established. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together OpenClaw selects an agent runtime from the configured model and authentication route. The commit message includes the exact finding title, complete quoted paragraph, and original review link.

The shared lifecycle now captures an assertion tied to the original lease owner and checks its phase, persisted token, and expiry. The Agents API adapter carries it into native request dispatch, cleanup cancellation, and transcript publication. Normal work retains host generation/run authority; cleanup retains harness lifetime and exact live lease authority so an authorized interruption can still cancel after host retirement.

Validation:
- Fresh independent source review: CLEAN.
- Formatting, targeted lint, Agents API package type checking after canonical SDK declaration regeneration, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Real native Linux/arm64 Docker probes used production SQLite state and the production client, with no mocks or fakes. Expired leases were rejected synchronously, and the fixed client rejected an expired owner's request.
- Full successor-command/cancellation and native interruption checks remain **blocked**. Both the baseline probe and the fixed probe's bounded retry failed before any VM command executed. Canonical native API reads returned idle sessions and failed root turns with:
  ```text
  code: rate_limit_exceeded
  message: You've exceeded the rate limit. Please slow down and try again later.
  ```

This is direct lifecycle/client proof, not a fresh registered-Gateway or transcript-publication E2E pass. The existing Gateway was preserved and was not restarted.

Real packaged Docker end-to-end proof for the completion-hook repair:

The runtime package was built from `64e5ac4638a4e5c944a63f129ac1e57ba53d5b13` and ran as native `linux/arm64`. The final PR head `b549ee1963ac659cf8226bd96fb958cf24baa06e` differs only in the two generated plugin reference pages; Git verified that runtime code and dependencies are unchanged. Existing Gateways were preserved.

| Real Gateway flow | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh hosted Linux session | VM command returned Linux and the unique marker with exit code 0; root successful and native session idle. |
| Steering during an active VM command | Native command item was `in_progress`, original root remained active, steered command really executed with exit code 0; root successful and native session idle. |
| Authorized interruption during an active VM command | Gateway acknowledged the original run cancellation; native root cancelled, session idle, completion hook success false. |
| Queued follow-up cancellation | Actual Gateway wait reported `pending`, `timeoutPhase: queue`, `providerStarted: false`; cancellation targeted only that queued run. The same original VM command remained active, completed with exit code 0, and the cancelled input never appeared in native history. |
| Typed completion hooks | Exactly one `llm_output` and one `agent_end` for each original run, matched to its real session. Successful assistant text matched the canonical native final text and Gateway transcript. |

No local unit tests, mocks, or fakes were used. Commands, cancellation, native settlement and hook receipts were observed directly; assistant claims were not accepted as proof.

Known accounting limitation, separate from repaired hook delivery: the observed native terminal event has `usage: null`; the later native REST record has token usage. OpenClaw currently projects the missing event usage as default zero counters, and the hook faithfully forwards that attempt result. This proof does not establish correct token accounting.

Supplemental genuine native-binding proof also passed. An independent SQLite connection used BEGIN/ROLLBACK contention to prevent renewal; persisted tokens and expiry were not rewritten. After natural expiry, the production shared owner generated a new token for the same binding. Fresh retained stale cleanup cancellation, native cancellation, send and steering attempts created no POSTs while the exact successor VM command remained in progress. The same canonical command then completed with actual Linux output and exit code 0; the new native turn completed and the session became idle. Old-owner retirement preserved the replacement token; normal replacement release preserved the binding.

The strict transcript writer replayed the actual completed Gateway assistant artifact with only a fresh proof idempotency key. No assistant output or host authority was fabricated.

This supplemental proof calls the actual installed backend clients and public shared owners.
